# Success
<!--
Projects should have a definition of done that is measurable, and a
thorough understanding going in of what the risks are to delivery
-->

## Definition of done
<!--
What does success look like?
-->

All four milestones are completed, package published on CRAN, and the joint blog post with the R Consortium is published.


## Measuring success
<!--
How will we know when success is achieved, what markers can we use
along the way
-->

Correctness is measured against {sf}. Every operation shared with {sf} is tested to return the same result, and those tests run on every commit.

Performance is measured against the other engines available in R. The package's website includes a replication of the [duckspatial benchmark](https://cidree.github.io/duckspatial/articles/benchmark.html) to compare geoarrowrs, sedonadb, and duckspatial. In addition, there will be a geoarrowrs implementation of Apache Sedona [SpatialBench](https://github.com/apache/sedona-spatialbench) for a reference.

## Future work
<!--
How could this be extended / developed in the future by yourself
and/or the community in general?
-->

This work, particularly the compatibility with {sf} will prove how to make the {sf} package truly agnostic to the geometry engine provided.
The findings in this work will directly lead to potential completion and development of the [`{sdf}`](https://github.com/JosiahParry/sdf) R package.
